capabilities: Plan to-dos into free time slots on a 12-hour spiral dial, re-planning as time passes
Track actual task time and compare planned vs actual in daily and 30-day reviews
Read local AI agent session logs and show sessions, tokens and progress as rings and rows
Display read-only events from macOS Calendar and Google Calendar as fixed events
Mark main quests, run focus timers, and show capacity and unrecorded time
extras: Not yet in the community directory; installed manually or via BRAT. Desktop only and macOS-focused: calendar, dialogs, sounds, focus prompts, game tracking and widgets are macOS-only, and Windows/Linux are untested. The full usage guide is in Chinese only. No telemetry and nothing to pay for.
intentEvidence: Obsidian already has two ports of the Nautilus line: Nautilus Log and Nautilus Logger.
motivation: The author extends the Nautilus/Nautilus Log time-budget idea ('give every minute a job') by handing part of the time record to the machine, reading agent session logs as a passive record alongside the user's own plan.
problem: Obsidian has no automatic day planner that fills free time with to-dos from a task list, re-plans as time passes, and compares planned against actual time in the daily note.

relations.evidence: Nautilus by Tomáš Baránek, and its descendants Nautilus Enhanced and Nautilus Log, for the spiral day planner
The capacity figures, the hatched unrecorded time, the daily review, free-slot hover, the status bar timer and playback follow the rules
Plus Agent Deck | Agent records: automatic journal logging, status write-back, 💬, desktop child / side chat / subagent blocks
Install Telegram Companion next to it and your phone becomes the remote
Start a task with a timer and, optionally, a Raycast Focus session
The time-budget idea goes back to the YNAB Method; this plugin is not affiliated with YNAB

requires.name: Google account with own OAuth client
AI agent CLIs/apps (Claude Code, Codex, WorkBuddy, DeepSeek Harness, Antigravity)

summary: Spiral day planner that reads the daily note, schedules tasks into free time slots, tracks actual time, and draws AI agent session activity as inner rings.
